record.paper_title: Two Open Problems for Absolutely Convergent Dirichlet Series
record.context_brief: Analogue of Theorem A or Proposition 1 for S^0(Λ)
record.original_question: Let S^0(Λ) denote the class of Dirichlet series absolutely convergent in the half-plane {z∈ℂ: Re z<0}. Develop for S^0(Λ) an analogue of Theorem A or Proposition 1 from the paper. Concretely, determine hypotheses under which one can prove for F∈S^0(Λ) a no-exceptional-set upper estimate of the same kind as the S_ψ(Λ) estimates in Theorem A or Proposition 1, namely bounds comparing M(x,F)=sup_t |F(x+it)| to the maximal term μ(x,F)=max_n |a_n|e^{xλ_n} through expressions such as μ(x,F)h(ln μ(x,F)) or the stronger Proposition 1 type bound μ(x,F)h(xd(x)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda=(\lambda_n)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers with $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_n<\lambda_{n+1}\to\infty$. For a real number $a$, let $\Pi_a=\{z=\sigma+it\in\mathbb{C}:\sigma<a\}$ and let $S_a(\Lambda)$ denote the class of Dirichlet series 
$$F(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n e^{z\lambda_n}$$
which converge absolutely in $\Pi_a$. For such $F$, define the maximum modulus and the maximal term
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|F(x+it)|, \qquad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\ge 0}|a_n|e^{x\lambda_n}.$$
Let $L$ denote the class of positive continuous functions $\psi$ on $[0,\infty)$ which are nondecreasing to $+\infty$, and let $L_0\subset L$ consist of those $\psi$ for which $\psi(x)/x\to 0$. For $\psi\in L$, set
$$S_\psi(\Lambda)=\{F\in S_0(\Lambda):\ \ln\mu(x,F)\le \psi(x)\ \text{for all sufficiently large } x<0\ \text{(in the appropriate variable)}\}$$
and consider $S^0(\Lambda)$, the class of Dirichlet series of the above form that converge absolutely in the half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} z<0\}$.

Two known results for the classes $S_\psi(\Lambda)$ assert:

(A) Under appropriate growth conditions on $\psi\in L$ and $h\in L_0$ relating $\Lambda$ and $\psi$, one has the equivalence: for every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exists $x_0$ such that for all $x\ge x_0$,
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(\ln\mu(x,F)).$$

(B) Under analogous conditions, one has the stronger statement: for every $d\in L_0$ and every $F\in S_\psi(\Lambda)$ there exists $x_0$ such that for all $x\ge x_0$,
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(x\,d(x)).$$

The problem is: formulate and prove an analogue of (A) or (B) for the class $S^0(\Lambda)$. Specifically, identify hypotheses on $\Lambda$ and on auxiliary functions $h$ (and possibly $d$) under which, for every $F\in S^0(\Lambda)$, a no-exceptional-set upper bound of the form
$$M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(\ln\mu(x,F)) \quad\text{or}\quad M(x,F)<\mu(x,F)\,h(x\,d(x))$$
holds for all $x$ sufficiently close to $0$ from the left (i.e. as $x\to 0^-$).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for analogues of the Theorem A / Proposition 1 maximum-modulus vs. maximal-term estimates for the class of Dirichlet series absolutely convergent in the left half-plane $\{\operatorname{Re} z<0\}$ did not turn up a definitive resolution. No paper explicitly stating an analogue for $S^0(\Lambda)$ was located, so the current status of the problem is unclear from accessible sources.
